playbooks.title: Injury on site

steps.do: Tap stop on every device near the incident. Nobody films an injury.
Help the person. Call site medical staff. If it is serious, call an ambulance; do not wait for permission.
Call the Portfolio Manager: where, what happened, who is hurt, how they are, whether an ambulance was called.
Get to the site. Stay with the person until medical staff take over. Keep the floor calm.
Call Moharam and Adham with what happened and how the person is. Moharam takes the site owner.
Make the spot safe before anyone films there again: PPE, cables, tethers on any elevated work. If the site's setup caused it, filming there stays off until it is fixed.
Write it down while it is fresh: what happened, who saw it, what changed. It goes in the wrap report tonight. A phone that fell from height is its own incident line.

tell.by: Now, from the anchor
Now, from the anchor
Within 30 minutes, from the Portfolio Manager
Same day, in the wrap report, for the paperwork and any insurance claim

playbooks.never: Never keep recording. An injury overrides every rule, the cycle included.

playbooks.title: Theft or vehicle loss

steps.do: Get yourself safe. If anyone is hurt, the injury playbook comes first. Then call Moharam: where you are, what happened, the count on the manifest.
Locate every device on the manifest in MDM. Location tracking was on in transit; use it.
Put every device on the manifest in lost mode. A locked phone is worth nothing to whoever has it.
File the police report. The runner goes in with the manifest and the commercial register copy.
Open the insurance claim with the police report, the manifest, and the registry rows. Mark each row lost.
Send the site replacements from the 10% spare pool so it films tomorrow at full count.
Wipe every device still unrecovered. Close its registry row.
Review the run: was it a third or less of the site, was the case locked and unmarked, was custody signed, was it before 11 PM. Any deduction follows the handbook, and only after this review.

tell.by: Now, from the runner
Same hour, from Moharam, for the claim and the replacements
Same hour, so the site knows what is coming back and when
Same day, from Moharam

playbooks.never: Never wipe first. Locate, lock, give it 24 hours, then wipe. A wiped phone cannot be found.

playbooks.title: Police checkpoint
playbooks.first: Pull over and stay calm. The letter does the talking.

steps.do: Hand over the Arabic company letter, the copy of the commercial register, and the manifest. That is what they are asking for.
Say what it is in plain words: company phones, going between a company site and the company's upload facility. Give the exact count. Point to the two numbers on the letter.
Call Moharam from the checkpoint: where you are, who is asking, what they want.
Take the officer's call. Confirm the runner, the company, and the count. If asked what the work is: video for a robotics research program, nothing more.
If the devices are held, get a written receipt: count, who holds them, where. Do not drive off without it.
Go with counsel and the company documents to get held devices released.
Count every device back against the manifest and log the custody event. Registry, MDM, and physical must match.
Log the checkpoint: where, when, what was asked, what was shown. Runners on that road tomorrow need to know.

tell.by: Now, from the checkpoint
Same hour, if any device or paper is held
Same hour, if the phones will be late, so the site plans without them
Same day, from Mano, if devices are held

playbooks.never: Never argue and never hide the count. The letter and the manifest do the talking.

playbooks.title: Upload outage at a hub
playbooks.first: Divert tonight's runs to the second hub.

steps.do: Confirm it is the line. Power-cycle the router and switch once. If uploads do not resume, call Mano.
Open the ISP ticket. Get a ticket number and a promised time.
Send every run not yet delivered to the second hub. Each runner hears it before leaving the site. Runs still end at 11 PM.
Move the phones sitting on the dead hub to the second hub on the same runs, a new manifest in each case. Phones already showing zero pending go back to their sites as normal.
Count backlog in device-days per site for the wrap report. Any site over one device-day is its own incident.
Before any phone leaves the second hub in the morning, confirm on the dashboard that its uploads completed. A phone leaves empty or it does not leave.
Still down after 24 hours: open the tested day-pass location and route the overflow there. When the ticket closes, measure the line before the next run lands on it.

tell.by: Now, from the hub attendant
Same hour, from Mano. He owns the outcome.

tell.who: Every Portfolio Manager with a hub site
tell.by: Same hour, so their runners know where to drive
Same day, in the executive sync. Past 24 hours, the same hour.

playbooks.never: Never upload through someone's home to get around it. A tested hub or a day-pass location, nothing else.

playbooks.title: Power cut
playbooks.first: Get the router onto the UPS. Keep the cycles running.

steps.do: Check the router and switch are on the UPS and lit. If not, move them now.
steps.owner: Anchor at a site, hub attendant at a hub

steps.do: Keep the cycles running. Phones record on battery. If the site itself stops work, tap stop; idle footage is fraud.
Tell the Portfolio Manager: which site, when the power went, how long the site expects, how many phones are low on battery.
Swap low phones for charged spares. Any phone with a storage warning is flushed first when the power returns.
At a hub, uploads keep going on battery. If the cut is still on when runs are due, Moharam sends them to the second hub.
The UPS carries a router for hours, not days. If the cut outlasts it, the site is a hub site tonight: a third of the phones per run, custody signed, before 11 PM.
Count backlog in device-days at shift end for the wrap report. Any site over one device-day is its own incident.
Recharge or replace the UPS before it is needed again. One that ran flat tonight is empty on Thursday night.
steps.owner: Portfolio Manager, with Mano for a replacement

tell.by: Same hour, from the anchor
Same hour, if runs need diverting or the UPS will not last the shift
Same day, for a replacement UPS or a hub question
Same day, in the executive sync, if hours were lost

playbooks.never: Never let a phone sleep full because the power went. The runner and the hub exist for this night.

playbooks.title: An account ban wave
playbooks.first: Pull the banned accounts off the floor. Tell QC and Moharam within the hour.

steps.do: Sit the wearer down. Nobody films on a banned account and nobody logs in on someone else's.
Tell Youssef Medhat and Moharam: which site, which accounts, which sessions.

Pull the sessions behind each ban and name the pattern: idle, hat off while recording, camera at the torso or floor, staged tasks, screen recording, filming someone else. Match each session to a wearer through the wearer log.
Walk the floor. Check every rig angle, every hat, every wearer on their own account. Fix what the pattern says and retrain on the spot.
Look for the same pattern on every other site. If it is there, every Portfolio Manager fixes it today.
Remove any wearer whose ban is fraud. They do not come back under any name or on any device. Deductions follow the handbook.
New accounts only for new people, through onboarding screening. A banned account is never reused.

tell.by: Same hour, from the Portfolio Manager
Same day, from Youssef Medhat
Same day, from Moharam, with the pattern and the fix. He owns anything the client says about it.
Same day, for the wearer log, the removals, and any new accounts through the gate

playbooks.never: Never re-enroll a removed worker and never recycle an account. Not under a new name, not on a new device.

playbooks.title: A suspected minor at a site
playbooks.first: No device on them. Not for one cycle.

steps.do: Do not hand them a device. If they are wearing one, tap stop and take it off now.
Tell the Portfolio Manager: site, who assigned them, whether any footage was recorded.
Check the wearer log and the ID on file. The ID number carries the birth date. No ID on file means they never passed the gate.
If any footage was recorded, pull the device. Send the device number, the account, and the shift times to Youssef Medhat.
Find every session from that wearer and delete it before it reaches the client. Confirm to the Portfolio Manager and Mano when it is done.
Tell Mano: site, who assigned them, device, account, whether footage was recorded. If the site pushed the person on us, tell Moharam too; he takes it up with the site.
Walk the gate again for every wearer on that site: ID on file, consent signed, in the wearer log. If one slipped through, others may have.

tell.by: Now, from the anchor
Same hour, if any footage was recorded
Same day, always. He runs the gate.
Same day, if the site pushed the person on us
Same day, from Mano, if any footage reached the client

playbooks.never: Never take a site's word for an age. Nobody films without an ID on file, no matter who assigned them.

playbooks.title: A client complaint
playbooks.first: Say nothing to the client. Send it to Moharam now.

steps.do: Do not reply. Send the complaint to Moharam as it came: who sent it, what it says, how it reached you.
Take the conversation. Ask the client for session IDs, accounts, and dates so the search is exact.
Find the sessions: site, device, wearer through the wearer log, what our review said at the time. Say plainly whether we missed it.
Check whether the same thing is live on any other site. If it is, every Portfolio Manager fixes it today.
Correct the floor: retrain the wearer, fix the rig, change the rotation, or pull the worker on a third flag. Within 24 hours of the complaint, not at the next sync.
Report back to Adham: sessions found, cause, what changed, what was deleted.
Close it with the client. One reply: what happened, what changed. The Monday update carries the follow-through.

tell.by: Now, from whoever it reached
Same hour, from Moharam. He owns every word to the client.
Same hour, to find the sessions
Same day, with the sessions and the correction
Same day, if it is about the collection app, exports, or data handling

playbooks.never: Never contact the client. Not to say sorry, not to explain, not to ask. Adham does.

playbooks.title: A partner dispute
playbooks.first: Promise nothing on the spot. Call Moharam.

steps.do: Listen. Write down who raised it, what they said, whether filming is paused. Promise nothing.
Call Moharam with the note. Partner complaints do not wait for the daily sync.
Take the relationship. Talk to the partner and settle what is operational: access, shifts, staff, phones.
Take the money. Payment, hours, and fees go to Mano and nobody else. Everyone is paid on accepted hours net of fraud flags; that does not move.
Count the partner's devices in MDM against the registry today. Payments hold until the count matches.
If it is about the terms or an exit, bring in Adham. Founders close; Moharam and Mano do not renegotiate.

If it ends, start the exit today: a return date no later than 7 days out, every device counted back against the registry and MDM with a condition tick. MDM is the leverage: lost mode on anything not back on day 7. Final payment after the count matches.
Keep the hours safe. If filming is paused, move phones and people where the hours are, and say so in the wrap report.

tell.by: Now, from the Portfolio Manager
Same day, for anything about money or devices
Same day, from Moharam. He owns the contract and decides whether the founders step in.
Same day, to run the count

playbooks.never: Never let a payment go out while the device count is open. It is in the agreement for exactly this moment.
